title: KV sector bin rebalancer and spill-trim heuristic to reduce inter-sector fragmentation
author: Jordan Kim
description: Motivation: We observed two recurring production patterns: 1) small hot objects clustered by tenant creating high inter-sector fragmentation (many small free gaps inside sectors) which prevents large contiguous allocations and causes frequent spillover to disk, and 2) spillovers that write long tail fragments with low reuse value, increasing io and compaction overhead. This PR introduces a low-risk allocator-side mitigation that rebalances 'bins' at sector granularity and a spill-trim heuristic that preferentially trims low-reuse fragments before persisting, reducing spill volume and IO bursts. Summary of changes: - Add a sector-level bin rebalancer that maintains a lightweight occupancy histogram per sector and periodically migrates small objects between nearby sectors to coalesce free space. The rebalancer operates opportunistically under low CPU utilization and respects tenant isolation budgets. - Introduce an allocation histogram module that records allocation/retirement sizes per sector and exposes a compact 8-bin summary for decision making. - Implement a spill-trim heuristic: before triggering spill-to-disk, the engine will try to reclaim fragments with low reuse score and short TTLs from the sector's soft free list, trimming spill size by up to the configured percentage. - Kernel selection hint: when fragmentation is high, the runtime prefers the small-block optimized kernel path to reduce allocation latency variance. - Scheduler tweak: continuous batching now scores in-flight requests by prefix-KV reuse to bias batches toward reuse-friendly requests (improves cache hit rates during rebalancing phases). Checklist: - [x] Design doc and microbenchmarks attached (see ENG-4820) - [x] Unit tests for histogram and rebalancer - [x] Integration test for spill-trim effect under synthetic churn - [x] Bench harness: bench/kv_fragmentation_bench.py - [x] Backwards-compatible config knobs with safe defaults (disabled for small deployments) High-level commit summary: - Commit 1: iterator: add sector occupancy histogram and APIs - Commit 2: allocator: expose soft_free_list and low_reuse dequeue - Commit 3: rebalancer: opportunistic sector bin rebalancer implementation - Commit 4: spill: add spill-trim heuristic and config flag - Commit 5: runtime: kernel selection hint plumbing + tests - Commit 6: scheduler: continuous-batcher reuse scoring + benchmarks - Commit 7: docs: config and operational guidance Changed areas (representative): - src/kv/allocator/histogram.rs - src/kv/allocator/sectors.rs - src/kv/allocator/rebalancer.rs - src/kv/spill/spill_manager.rs - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp - runtime/kernel/selection.h - tests/unit/kv_histogram_tests.rs - tests/integration/kv_spill_trim_integ.py - bench/kv_fragmentation_bench.py - docs/ops/kv-rebalancer.md - cargo.toml - build/CI/pipeline.yml Testing & benchmarks: - Unit tests cover binning edge cases, tenant budget enforcement, and spill-trim selection logic. - Integration runs simulate a mixed-size churn workload (80% small writes, 20% medium writes) across 3 tenants. Results: median spill volume reduced by 37%, 95th-percentile spill IO latency reduced by ~22%, and mean allocation latency improved by 8% under high fragmentation. There is a small CPU overhead (≈2%) when rebalancer is active; it is gated behind a config knob and only runs when host CPU idle > 15% and tenant budget allows. Rollout & config: - Feature gated via kv.rebalancer.enabled and kv.spill_trim.enabled (default: true for internal staging, false for small-hosted tiers). - Rebalancer has per-tenant budget (kv.rebalancer.cpu_ms_per_minute) to prevent noisy neighbor effects. - Safe default thresholds chosen from benchtop: occupancy variance threshold = 0.18, spill_trim_target = 0.25. Operational notes (docs/ops/kv-rebalancer.md): - How to interpret rebalancer metrics (migrations/sec, reclaimed_bytes, tenant_budget_util) - Recommended canary pattern: enable on 10% of traffic, monitor reclaimed_bytes / spill_bytes ratio and allocation latency. Review conversation (high level): - Maya Patel: "Design looks solid; two concerns: 1) how do we prevent oscillation if rebalancer moves objects back/forth and 2) can we limit memory amplification during migration?" - Jordan Kim (author): "Added hysteresis in rebalancer (min identity hold time = 30s) and migration uses a staging buffer bounded by tenant_budget to avoid amplification; detailed in allocator/sectors.rs comments." - Diego Alvarez: "Please add a test that simulates repeated rebalances to catch oscillation. Also verify metrics emission for tenant_budget." - Jordan Kim: "Added a flapping_sim test and emitted tenant_budget metrics (included in unit tests)." - Priya Narang: "What happens if spill-trim selects fragments that the application expects to be persistent? Any risk to correctness?" - Jordan Kim: "We only trim from soft_free_list where objects are already logically freed; no live object trimming. For persisted KV entries we never trim; the heuristic is limited to ephemeral cache fragments and honored only when fragmentation-induced spill would exceed threshold." - Diego Alvarez: "CI flaky failure on macOS-asan in the rebalancer stress test — looks like a race in the migration queue. Marked a requested change." - Jordan Kim: "Fixed race by adding the per-sector migration token and a short lock-free handoff; re-ran CI." CI & status: - Initial CI run: failed on macOS-asan stress test (race) - Fixes applied and rerun - Final CI: pass (all checks green) Merge strategy and outcome: - Squash merge after approvals from reviewers and green CI. - Post-merge: deployed to staging fleet with phased rollout; no regressions observed in the first 72h canary. Release notes (operator-facing): "Introduce sector bin rebalancer to proactively reduce inter-sector fragmentation and a spill-trim heuristic to decrease spill-to-disk volume. Defaults are safe; operators can tune kv.rebalancer.* and kv.spill_trim.* knobs. See docs/ops/kv-rebalancer.md for guidance and metrics to watch." Notes and follow-ups: - Monitor reclaimed_bytes / migrations/sec and ensure tenant_budget_util stays < 0.8 - Plan follow-up: ENG-5054 to explore cross-tenant migration avoidance and learning-based threshold tuning - Small refactor planned to expose rebalancer telemetry to Prometheus label set (ENG-5061)
